result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.knotty_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the connective core of the network using knotty centrality. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L34104-L34167){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.knotty_centrality( top_m=10, compact=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Knotty centrality](/assets/graphs/knotty-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with its connective core, the hub C and the bridge E, in accent inside a shaded hull, joined by the accent edge C-E. The pair is fully connected (density 1) and holds 0.25 and 0.40 of all betweenness, so the card reads a knotty score of 0.325." width="100%"} Knotty centrality identifies the subset of nodes that are both densely interconnected *and* collectively high in betweenness centrality. The result is the tightest "knot" of important connectors in the graph. The score for a subset *S* is: `KC(S) = density(S) * (1 / |S|) * sum(bc_norm(i) for i in S)` where `density(S) = 2 * E_S / (|S| * (|S| - 1))` and `bc_norm` is betweenness centrality normalized to sum to 1 over the whole graph. Uses a two-phase heuristic: exhaustive search over the top-`top_m` nodes by betweenness, followed by gradient ascent over the full node set. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [top_m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of top-betweenness nodes to include in the exhaustive search phase. Higher values find better solutions but cost `O(2^top_m)`. Default is `10`. [compact]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, penalizes larger subsets: `KCC(S) = KC(S) * (N - |S|) / N`. Default is `False`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[float, list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `(score, core_node_ids)` tuple. The score is the knotty-centrality value (range `[0, 1]`) and `core_node_ids` is the sorted list of node IDs in the connective core. Returns `(0.0, [])` for graphs with fewer than 2 nodes or zero betweenness centrality. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The bridge nodes connecting two triangles form the connective core: ::: {#a021b138 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) .add_edge("C", "D") # Bridge .add_edges([("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) score, core = graph.knotty_centrality() labels = [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in core] (round(score, 4), labels) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.5, ['C', 'D']) ``` ::: :::
